prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a secure S3 bucket infrastructure for an application named "testanu", designed to pass default security scanning checks and provide a robust, auditable storage solution with cross-region replication and access logging. The main bucket should be named using the pattern testanu-<region>-<account-id> and must have server-side encryption enabled using AES256, versioning enabled, and all public access blocked through the public access block configuration. A bucket policy must be attached to this main bucket that denies all s3 actions when secure transport is not used, and it should allow the logging service to write objects by granting s3:PutObject permission when the source ARN matches the main bucket and the source account matches the current account. An access log bucket named testanu-logs-<region>-<account-id> must be created with server-side encryption using AES256, versioning enabled, object lock enabled in compliance mode with a default retention period of one year, and all public access blocked; this log bucket should also have a bucket policy that denies insecure transport and permits the logging service to write objects under the same conditions as the main bucket. A replica bucket named testanu-replicas-<region>-<account-id> must be created with server-side encryption using AES256, versioning enabled, all public access blocked, and a bucket policy that denies insecure transport and allows the logging service to write objects. Replication must be configured on the main bucket to replicate all objects to the replica bucket, and this requires an IAM role named ObjectStorageReplicationRole that trusts the s3.amazonaws.com service to assume the role, along with a managed policy named bucket-replication-policy attached to that role granting permissions to get replication configuration and list the main bucket, get object versions for replication, and replicate objects, deletes, and tags to the replica bucket. The log bucket should be set as the logging destination for the main bucket.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a regional REST API Gateway endpoint for sending emails via Amazon SES, protected by an API key and a usage plan that throttles at 500 requests per second with a burst limit of 1000 and a monthly quota of 10,000 emails. The integration must use an IAM role with a policy allowing ses:SendEmail on all resources, and transform the incoming JSON payload into the Amazon SES SendEmail action using a Velocity template that maps the "from" field to the Source, iterates over "to", "cc", and "bcc" arrays to populate the corresponding destination members, and sets the "subject", "text", and "html" fields accordingly. The API deployment should use a stage name of "dev" by default, and the API key should be named "email-apikey" by default, with the usage plan also named "usage-plan". The output should expose the full API Gateway endpoint URL in the format https://{api-id}.execute-api.{region}.amazonaws.com/dev/.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a simple Hello World Lambda function using Node.js 20.x, intended for demonstration or testing purposes. We need a CloudFormation template that creates an IAM role named CloudFormationStackEmissionReader, along with an associated IAM policy, to allow the infosec-trusted AWS account with ID 415589142697 to assume this role and query the cloudformation-stack-emissions DynamoDB table (ARN arn:aws:dynamodb:us-west-2:371522382791:table/cloudformation-stack-emissions) in order to retrieve incident response-related IAM role ARNs for security response operations. The trust policy must permit the sts:AssumeRole action from the principal arn:aws:iam::415589142697:root, and the attached policy should grant only the necessary read actions—dynamodb:GetItem, dynamodb:BatchGetItem, and dynamodb:Query—on the table and its items, with a condition that restricts attribute retrieval to the specific list: aws-account-id, id, category, InfosecIncidentResponseRoleArn, InfosecIncidentResponseRoleName, BreakGlassSNSTopicArn, BreakGlassSNSTopicName, stack-id, stack-name, region, last-updated, and logical-resource-id, and also enforces the use of SPECIFIC_ATTRIBUTES for the Select parameter when present. We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Fargate-based service running a Spring Boot application in a private subnet behind an internal load balancer, using a Docker image from Amazon ECR with the URL 016973021151.dkr.ecr.ca-central-1.amazonaws.com/ecs-repository:ungerw-springboot-docker_latest, listening on container port 8080, with 512 CPU units and 1024 MB of memory, and the template should import networking resources from a parent stack named Fargate-VPC including the VPC ID, private subnets, cluster name, container security group, ECS task execution role, and the private listener ARN, while also allowing an optional custom IAM role for the task if the containers need to access other AWS services, and it must create a task definition using the Fargate launch type with awsvpc network mode, an ECS service with a desired count of 2 tasks, a deployment configuration allowing up to 200% during updates and maintaining at least 75% healthy instances, and assign public IPs to the tasks while placing them in the two private subnets imported from the parent stack, along with a target group that performs health checks on the path /spring-docker/hello every 6 seconds with a 5-second timeout, a healthy threshold of 2, and an unhealthy threshold of 2, using HTTP protocol on port 8080 with target type ip, and a listener rule that forwards all traffic matching the path pattern * to the target group with priority 1, and finally output the service URL by concatenating the internal URL imported from the parent stack with the health check path.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an Amazon Security Lake deployment to centralize and store security logs from multiple AWS services, with an optional cross-account subscriber for a SIEM solution. The template must accept an AuditAccountId parameter, which defaults to an empty string, and if a valid account ID is provided, it should conditionally create an S3-based subscriber named Audit that grants that account access to all log sources using the principal ID from the parameter and an external ID of SIEM. The deployment must include an IAM role named using the LogicalName parameter (defaulting to SecurityLake) followed by -SecurityLake and the region, with a path of /service-role/, and it must be attached to the AWS managed policy AmazonSecurityLakeMetastoreManager, with a trust policy allowing the Lambda service to assume the role. The core resource is a DataLake that references the IAM role’s ARN for the metastore manager, and it must sequentially ingest logs from the following AWS sources in this exact order: CLOUD_TRAIL_MGMT (version 2.0), LAMBDA_EXECUTION (version 2.0), EKS_AUDIT (version 2.0), ROUTE53 (version 2.0), SH_FINDINGS (version 2.0), and VPC_FLOW (version 2.0), with each log source depending on the previous ones to ensure proper ordering. The subscriber, when created, must include all six log sources and be configured with an SQS notification configuration for event delivery. All resources must be tagged with an environment tag whose value comes from the Environment parameter (allowed values: production, test, development, defaulting to production), and a custom tag pair where the key defaults to createdby and the value defaults to aws-cloudformation-templates. The template should also expose a LogicalName parameter defaulting to SecurityLake to serve as a custom prefix for the IAM role name.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an AWS Route 53 Application Recovery Controller setup for cross-region application failover, including a cluster named AppFailover-Cluster, a control panel named AppFailover-ControlPanel associated with that cluster, and two routing controls named AppFailover-us-east-1 and AppFailover-us-west-2, both linked to the same cluster and control panel, along with three SSM Parameters to store the cluster ARN under the path /app-failover/arc-cluster, the us-east-1 routing control ARN under /app-failover/arc-control-us-east-1, and the us-west-2 routing control ARN under /app-failover/arc-control-us-west-2, and the template must also export the cluster ARN with the export name app-failover-arc-cluster, the us-east-1 routing control ARN with the export name app-failover-arc-control-us-east-1, and the us-west-2 routing control ARN with the export name app-failover-arc-control-us-west-2.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a comprehensive set of CloudWatch Logs Insights queries and a corresponding CloudWatch dashboard for monitoring and reporting on AWS Client VPN usage, covering authentication methods including AD or SAML, Mutual Auth, and Mixed Auth. The template should accept two parameters: a Folder parameter defaulting to "aws-client-vpn" to organize the saved queries, and a ClientVPNLogGroup parameter defaulting to "aws/aws-client-vpn/prod" which specifies the log group containing the Client VPN connection logs. It must define twelve CloudWatch Logs QueryDefinition resources: one for total usage per Client VPN endpoint (aggregating connection counts, data transfer in MB, connection time in hours, and distinct users), five specifically for AD or SAML auth (total usage report, distinct users connection duration, distinct users list, and users connection duration), five for Mutual Auth (total usage report, users duration, distinct users, and distinct users connection duration), and one for Mixed Auth (total usage report, distinct users connection duration, distinct users, and users connection duration). Additionally, it must create a CloudWatch dashboard named using the region, "AWS-ClientVPN-Usage-Dashboard", which displays all these queries as table widgets arranged in a grid. The dashboard should source data from the specified Client VPN log group and include widgets for each of the twelve query views. Two outputs should be provided: the CloudWatch Logs Insights console URL and the dashboard URL, both region-specific. The template should use the Folder parameter as a prefix for the query names to allow flexible organization, and the default log group name should be used if no override is provided.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a comprehensive set of IAM roles and instance profiles required as shared prerequisites for deploying Amazon EKS clusters using the AWS Quick Start, designed to support both managed and unmanaged node groups, Fargate profiles, and various Lambda-based cleanup and configuration functions. The template must create a CopyZipsRole for Lambda to read objects from any S3 bucket, a GenerateClusterNameRole with basic Lambda execution permissions, a ResourceReaderRole that combines Lambda execution with ReadOnlyAccess, a CreateVpcRoleRole that can create and attach policies to a specific IAM role named CloudFormation-Kubernetes-VPC, a DeleteBucketContentsRole for Lambda execution, and a ControlPlaneRole for the EKS service that includes a custom policy allowing ec2:DescribeAccountAttributes, ec2:DescribeAddresses, and ec2:DescribeInternetGateways on all resources, along with the managed policies AmazonEKSClusterPolicy, AmazonEKSServicePolicy, and AmazonEKSVPCResourceController. Additionally, the template must include a CleanupLoadBalancersRole with permissions to describe and delete Elastic Load Balancers (including Application, Network, and Classic types) and manage associated EC2 network interfaces and security groups, a CleanupSecurityGroupDependenciesRole for cleaning up network interfaces and security groups, a CleanupLambdasRole that can list and delete Lambda functions, a GetCallerArnRole that can describe CloudFormation stacks and look up CloudTrail events, a RegisterTypeRole with broad permissions to register and manage CloudFormation resource types, create and pass IAM roles, manage IAM policies, read S3 objects, and manage SSM parameters, a NodeSGRole that can describe EKS node groups, a FargateExecutionRole that the eks-fargate-pods service can assume with the AmazonEKSFargatePodExecutionRolePolicy attached, a FargateProfileRole that can describe subnets and manage Fargate profiles with iam:PassRole and iam:GetRole permissions, a QuickStartParameterResolverRole that can read SSM parameters under the path /quickstart/amazon-eks/, and both UnmanagedNodeInstanceRole and ManagedNodeInstanceRole that EC2 instances can assume, each with a custom policy for cloudformation:SignalResource and the managed policies AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore, AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy, AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly, CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy, AmazonEBSCSIDriverPolicy, and conditionally AmazonElasticContainerRegistryPublicReadOnly only when the AWS partition is commercial. The template must also create UnmanagedNodeInstanceProfile and ManagedNodeInstanceProfile instance profiles that reference the respective roles, and a CloudFormationVPCRoleCreationRole that can create and attach policies to the CloudFormation-Kubernetes-VPC role. All roles that Lambda assumes must use the AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole managed policy, and all role names must follow the eks-quickstart- prefix convention. The template should include a condition named Commercial that checks if the AWS partition equals aws, and use it to conditionally include the public ECR read-only policy for the node instance roles.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates six AWS Systems Manager (SSM) parameters of type String, each storing a base64-encoded value, with the first four parameters deriving their content from a single user-supplied parameter named Param1 that defaults to "abc", the fifth parameter storing the base64-encoded literal string "literal", and the sixth parameter storing the base64-encoded multi-line literal string "literal" as well, and the template must output the name of the first SSM parameter as a stack output.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an IAM role to be assumed by CloudFormation during Hook operations on behalf of the customer, with a maximum session duration of 8400 seconds, a trust policy that allows the services hooks.cloudformation.amazonaws.com and resources.cloudformation.amazonaws.com to assume the role only when the source account matches the current AWS account and the source ARN follows the pattern arn:${AWS::Partition}:cloudformation:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:type/hook/AWSSamples-IamPoliciesRequireMfa-Hook/*, and a single inline policy named HookTypePolicy that denies all actions on all resources, serving as a placeholder or initial restrictive policy, and the template should output the ARN of the created role.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an automated image recognition pipeline where users can upload photos to an S3 bucket and receive an SMS notification if a human is detected in the image, using a default phone number of +14070000000. The solution must include an S3 bucket with an event notification configured to trigger a Lambda function on any object creation event, which then starts a Step Functions state machine execution, and the state machine must invoke two Lambda functions in sequence: the first uses Amazon Rekognition to detect labels with a minimum confidence of 75 percent and checks for the "Human" or "Person" label, and the second publishes an SNS message to the specified phone number if a human is found, otherwise it raises an exception. The architecture requires four IAM roles: one shared role for the Rekognition and notification Lambda functions with permissions for Rekognition detection, SNS publish, S3 get and list, and CloudWatch logs; a second role for the S3-triggered Lambda with basic execution permissions and a policy allowing it to start the state machine; a third role for the state machine itself with permissions to invoke both Lambda functions; and a fourth role for the S3-triggered Lambda that also needs a managed policy for basic execution. The S3 bucket must have a Lambda permission resource allowing the S3 service to invoke the trigger function, and to avoid a circular dependency where the bucket needs the permission to exist before its notification configuration can be validated, the permission's source ARN should be set loosely to "arn:aws:s3:::*" rather than pointing to the specific bucket ARN. The state machine definition must include a choice state that routes to the notification Lambda if a human is found or to a pass state for other detections, with a timeout of 300 seconds, and the trigger Lambda must read the state machine ARN from an environment variable. The template should output the S3 bucket reference so users know where to upload images.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an IAM OIDC provider for GitHub Actions using the URL https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com with the client ID sts.amazonaws.com and the thumbprint 6938fd4d98bab03faadb97b34396831e3780aea1, along with an IAM role named GithubActionsRole that can be assumed via web identity federation by any workflow from the guardian/facia-scala-client repository on GitHub, and an IAM policy attached to that role that grants s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket permissions on the S3 bucket facia-tool-store for objects under the DEV/ prefix and on the bucket itself, and finally output the ARN of the created role. We need a CloudFormation template that creates an automated EC2 Image Builder pipeline to produce a custom Amazon Linux 2023 ARM-based AMI hardened with CIS Level 1 benchmarks and pre-configured for Elastic Beanstalk compatibility, intended for sharing within an AWS Organization with ID o-69lcdj4kro and with two specific AWS accounts (449435941126 for Synapse dev and 325565585839 for Synapse prod). The template should include an IAM instance role with the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore and EC2InstanceProfileForImageBuilder managed policies attached, along with a corresponding instance profile under the path /executionServiceEC2Role/, to allow the build instance to communicate with Systems Manager and Image Builder. The pipeline must be enabled and scheduled to run daily, using an infrastructure configuration that references the instance profile, and should include image scanning enabled with tests enabled and a timeout of 720 minutes. The image recipe must use the CIS Level 1 hardened Amazon Linux 2023 ARM parent image from the Image Builder service, with a configurable version parameter defaulting to "0.0.0", and include a custom component that applies Elastic Beanstalk-specific fixes such as creating an xray user and group, setting rsyslog file creation mode to 0640, configuring journald to forward logs to rsyslog, setting SSH idle timeout to 300 seconds, limiting SSH MaxSessions to 10, enabling SSH PAM, setting a random root password, configuring password aging policies (warning 7 days, minimum 1 day, maximum 365 days, inactive lock 30 days), removing an orphaned empty directory at /var/lib/private/systemd/journal-upload, and pre-creating the webapp user with UID and GID 900 and shell set to /sbin/nologin. The recipe should use /root as the working directory and include a block device mapping for /dev/xvda with a configurable EBS volume size defaulting to 50 GB (range 8 to 500) and deletion on termination enabled. The distribution configuration must distribute the AMI only to the current region, tagging the AMI with the stack name, and granting launch permissions to the specified organization ARN and the two Synapse account IDs. A lifecycle policy must be created, enabled, and set to delete AMI images after a configurable number of months defaulting to 6 (range 1 to 60), using a dedicated IAM execution role for Image Builder with the EC2ImageBuilderLifecycleExecutionPolicy managed policy attached and the imagebuilder.amazonaws.com service as the trusted principal.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an automated, scheduled enforcement of S3 Block Public Access settings at the AWS account level using Systems Manager Automation, ensuring that all S3 buckets in the account are protected against public access. The solution must include a CloudWatch Events rule that triggers daily on a rate of 1 day and is enabled, targeting an SSM automation definition with a specific ARN pattern that includes the partition, region, and account ID, and this rule must assume an IAM role that allows CloudWatch Events to start automation executions via ssm:StartAutomationExecution on that specific automation definition resource. The SSM automation document itself must be of type Automation with schema version 0.3, and it must assume a dedicated IAM role for SSM to perform the actions; the document should have a single main step that calls the s3control PutPublicAccessBlock API to set BlockPublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, IgnorePublicAcls, and RestrictPublicBuckets all to true, using the global ACCOUNT_ID as the AccountId parameter, and this step should be the end of the automation. The IAM role for SSM must allow the s3:PutAccountPublicAccessBlock and s3:GetAccountPublicAccessBlock actions on all resources, and both IAM roles must have the appropriate trust policies for their respective services (events.amazonaws.com and ssm.amazonaws.com) with a path of "/". The template should not include any hardcoded email addresses, AMI IDs, or URLs, but it must use intrinsic functions like Ref, GetAtt, and Sub to dynamically reference the partition, region, and account ID, and the automation document should have a default parameter for the AutomationAssumeRole that defaults to the ARN of the SSM execution role.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a cross-region CodeCommit repository replication system using AWS CodeBuild and EventBridge, designed to automatically mirror three source repositories from the us-west-2 region to corresponding target repositories in the ap-northeast-2 region whenever changes are pushed to the mainline branch. The template must provision an IAM role for CodeBuild with the AWSCodeCommitFullAccess and CloudWatchLogsFullAccess managed policies attached, along with a custom inline policy that grants permissions for creating and writing CloudWatch log groups and streams under the /aws/codebuild/ prefix for the specific CodeBuild project, as well as permissions for CodeBuild report group operations including creating report groups, reports, updating reports, and batch putting test cases and code coverage data. The CodeBuild project itself should use a Linux container environment with the aws/codebuild/standard:4.0 image, BUILD_GENERAL1_SMALL compute type, no artifacts, and the default AWS S3 encryption key (alias/aws/s3), with a build specification that installs the git-remote-codecommit package via pip and then performs mirror clones of three repositories named card-service, rule-service, and ecs-pipeline from codecommit::us-west-2, updates the push origin URLs to point to codecommit::ap-northeast-2 for each respective repository, and executes git fetch and git push commands to replicate the full repository history. The template must also create a separate IAM role for EventBridge with a trust policy allowing events.amazonaws.com to assume the role, and an inline policy granting only the codebuild:StartBuild action scoped to the specific CodeBuild project ARN. Three EventBridge rules must be created, one for each source repository (card-service, rule-service, and ecs-pipeline), each with an event pattern that matches CodeCommit repository state changes from the aws.codecommit source, filtering for events of type referenceCreated or referenceUpdated on the mainline reference name, with the resource ARN pointing to the specific repository in us-west-2 with account ID 043490748814, and each rule targeting the CodeBuild project with the EventBridge role attached for invocation. The account ID 043490748814 must be used for all resource ARNs and log group paths, the region us-west-2 for source repositories and log groups, and ap-northeast-2 for the destination repositories in the build commands.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a custom resource backed by a Lambda function to perform a basic arithmetic operation on two numbers and return the result as a stack output, intended for demonstrating how to pass values to and from a custom resource and how to handle success or failure scenarios. The template must accept four parameters: a string parameter called DoYouWantToSucceed with a default of true and allowed values of true or false to control whether the custom resource succeeds or intentionally fails; a number parameter called FirstNumber with a default of 2; a number parameter called SecondNumber with a default of 2; and a string parameter called Operator with a default of "*" and allowed values of "+", "-", "*", and "/" to choose the arithmetic operation. The template must create an IAM role named using the stack name with a suffix of -CustomResourceRole that allows the Lambda service to assume it, and an IAM policy attached to that role granting permissions for logs:CreateLogGroup, logs:CreateLogStream, and logs:PutLogEvents on all resources. It must also create a Lambda function named using the stack name with a suffix of -CustomResourceLambda, using Python 3.11 runtime, 128 MB of memory, a timeout of 1 second, and an inline code handler that reads the doYouWantToSucceed, firstNumber, secondNumber, and operator properties from the event's ResourceProperties, and if doYouWantToSucceed is false, it sends a FAILED response with a reason of "We were asked to create a failure."; otherwise, for Create or Update requests, it calculates the result based on the operator (supporting multiplication, division, addition, and subtraction) and sends a SUCCESS response with the result. The Lambda function must use the cfnresponse module to send responses back to CloudFormation. The template must also create a custom resource of type Custom::helper that depends on the IAM policy and passes the ServiceToken as the Lambda function's ARN, along with the doYouWantToSucceed, firstNumber, secondNumber, and operator parameter values. Finally, the stack must output the result of the calculation by getting the result attribute from the custom resource.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an IAM role intended to be assumed by the CloudFormation resource provider service during CRUDL operations, specifically for a custom resource type called Community-Organizations-EnableAWSServiceAccess, so that the service can manage AWS Organizations service access on behalf of the customer. The role must have a maximum session duration of 8400 seconds and include a trust policy that allows the resources.cloudformation.amazonaws.com service principal to assume it, but only when the request originates from the same AWS account and when the source ARN matches the pattern for the CloudFormation registry type resource in the current partition, region, and account. The role should be assigned the path "/" and include a single inline policy named ResourceTypePolicy that grants permissions to perform the organizations:DisableAWSServiceAccess, organizations:EnableAWSServiceAccess, and organizations:ListAWSServiceAccessForOrganization actions on all resources. Finally, the template must output the ARN of the created execution role.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a complete EC2 Image Builder pipeline for building and managing custom AMIs, including a custom component that installs the Chef client from https://omnitruck.chef.io/install.sh and applies a recipe from a user-provided S3 bucket and object key, an image recipe that combines this custom component with the AWS-managed chrony time configuration component (both using placeholder version numbers that must be replaced with actual versions) and uses the Amazon Linux 2 ECS-optimized x86 parent image (also with a placeholder version), with a 30 GB gp2 root volume that is not encrypted and a working directory of /tmp, an IAM role and instance profile with AdministratorAccess for the EC2 instance used in the infrastructure configuration, which is set to terminate on failure, a distribution configuration that distributes the AMI to us-west-2 with launch permissions for the same account, an image pipeline scheduled to run daily at 9 AM UTC with the execution condition set to trigger only when dependency updates are available, with image scanning enabled, image tests enabled, and enhanced image metadata disabled, a lifecycle policy that deprecates AMIs older than 6 months and targets images tagged with Environment: Dev, using a separate IAM role with AdministratorAccess for the Image Builder service, and a custom build workflow that launches an instance, updates the SSM agent, applies build components, collects image metadata for AMIs, runs a sanitize script for Linux platforms, runs sysprep for Windows platforms, creates the output AMI, and terminates the instance, outputting the image ID.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an EC2 Image Builder pipeline to produce custom Amazon Linux 2023 AMIs for both x86 and arm64 architectures, pre‑installed with Docker, Docker Compose, Git, Python 3, and the synapseclient Python package (with pandas and pysftp extras), along with the latest system and Python package updates applied at boot. The template should include an IAM role with the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore and EC2InstanceProfileForImageBuilder managed policies, an instance profile using that role, and an infrastructure configuration referencing that profile. A custom Image Builder component named after the stack must run during the build phase to install the packages, enable the Docker service, add the ec2-user and ssm-user to the docker group, and grant ssm-user passwordless sudo access; the test phase should verify Docker Compose and the Python imports. Two image recipes (one for x86, one for arm64) should use the respective AWS‑provided parent images (amazon-linux-2023-x86 and amazon-linux-2023-arm64), include the AWS update-linux and amazon-cloudwatch-agent-linux components, attach the custom component, set the root EBS volume to a configurable size (default 32 GB, min 8, max 500) with encryption disabled, and override the user data to run dnf upgrade and pip upgrade on every boot. A distribution configuration must distribute the resulting AMIs to the current region, tag them with the stack name, grant launch permissions to the AWS Organization with ID `o-69lcdj4kro` (configurable via a parameter), and also make the AMIs globally public by including the `all` user group. Finally, two Image resources (one per architecture) should tie the recipes, infrastructure configuration, and distribution configuration together, with the image version parameter defaulting to `0.0.0`.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a foundational machine learning workshop infrastructure stack using Service Catalog products, designed to provision a VPC, S3 buckets with KMS encryption, IAM roles, and SSM parameters for configuration management, all with a consistent naming suffix of reinforce15. The template must first launch a Service Catalog product named "S3 buckets, KMS keys, and IAM roles" at version v2.1, passing the suffix as the S3PostfixUnique parameter, and after that product completes, provision a second Service Catalog product named "VPC" also at version v2.1, which depends on the first product and accepts parameters for two availability zone names defaulting to us-east-2a and us-east-2b, a VPC CIDR of 10.229.0.0/16, two private subnet CIDRs of 10.229.30.0/24 and 10.229.40.0/24, and a boolean flag for enabling VPC flow logs defaulting to true. After both Service Catalog products have been provisioned, the template must create a series of SSM parameters under the /MLWorkshop/ path, each using the suffix in the parameter name and extracting specific output values from the Service Catalog products: NotebookInstanceRole, SageMakerRole, GetNewRevisionRole, SubnetAPrivate, SubnetBPrivate, S3BucketData, S3BucketInfra, KMSKeyDataCapture, KMSKeyMLStorage, NotebookSecurityGroup, ModelSecurityGroup, and a composite S3 data capture path parameter constructed as s3:// followed by the S3BucketInfra output concatenated with data_capture_logs. The template should also expose outputs for the private subnets, all three IAM roles, both S3 buckets, and both KMS keys so that downstream stacks can reference them directly.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an IAM role for EC2 instances with a trust policy allowing the ec2.amazonaws.com service to assume the role, and attaches a customer-managed policy named S3Download that grants s3:ListBucket, s3:GetBucketLocation, and s3:GetObject permissions on the bucket arn:aws:s3:::cfnstore and on all objects under the path arn:aws:s3:::cfnstore/<CfnBucketName>/*, where CfnBucketName is a parameter with a default value of "platform".
